message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 220, "amount_cents": 9480}, {"order_id": 222, "amount_cents": 30660}, {"order_id": 223, "amount_cents": 23615}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger, so I'll start by listing the orders.
The orders list is in hand. Next I'll check the refund ledger to confirm that Alpha's three claimed refunds were actually applied.
The ledger matches Alpha's three claimed refunds exactly (220, 222, 223 with the same amounts), so the refund work checks out. Next I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.

Acme's net of 24929 matches my own check: orders 33101 + 24923 = 58024, minus refunds 9480 + 23615 = 33095. The ledger refunds are confirmed, so I'll record Acme's payout and then check the next customer.
Acme's payout is recorded and matched my own check. Next is birch, which has no refunds in the ledger, so I'll get its net balance and then verify it against the orders.
Birch's net of 30973 matches my check: orders 19628 + 11345 = 30973, with no refunds in the ledger. I'll record Birch's payout.

Acme and Birch are paid, so the only customer left is cobalt. Its orders are 222 (36677) and 225 (27011), and the ledger shows refund 222 (30660). I'll get cobalt's net balance and check it against that.

Cobalt's net of 33028 matches my check: orders 36677 + 27011 = 63688, minus refund 222 (30660) = 33028, and the ledger has no other cobalt refunds. All three refunds are verified, so I'll record Cobalt's payout.
All three customers (acme, birch, cobalt) have been paid, and each net balance matched my independent check against the orders and the refund ledger. No customers remain, so the batch is complete.
